evidence:
Shared restart-helper concern, explicitly deferred by the user according to the coordinator's instruction; it remains visible and is not a task-specific permission to edit the template. Four restart-dependent outcomes (cw_process_restart_durability, cw_process_restart_write, cw_history_restart, cw_restore_retry_restart) depend on a completed real restart: frozen task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:332-344,570-581 and prompt.md:425-433. Yet frozen task/tests/test.sh:153-159 sends SIGTERM, waits at most 50 x 0.1 seconds, and proceeds even if the old process group remains alive. Lines 160-177 launch a replacement without checking that process is alive and accept an HTTP response from whichever process owns port 3000; lines 179-183 return success solely from that readiness flag. frozen task/tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:45-47 then reports 'restart complete: the server was relaunched on the same database and answers HTTP'. Therefore browser readbacks after this message do not establish that persisted state crossed a process boundary. This is inherited shared code: task and frozen template test.sh both SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa; restart_mcp.py both 03c1426f00e451f4d86b7547761715328c63cdf299f5f812f46c9fa3b44979b5. No mutation or new runtime probe was performed.

Independently, I found no additional task-specific row-32 defect in the 80 Functional, 6 Polish, 6 Visual and 2 gate criteria. Functional prompt.md:7,13-25 confines evidence to rendered effects, entered product data and observed exchanges, with positive controls and explicit tooling-failure handling. S10 at 273-286 distinguishes actual last-good input state from source rerunning; S36 at 449-459 uses bounded visible effects without a hidden termination claim; S37 at 463-472 observes immutable fields, genuine dirty drafts, actual lost-reply UI retry and fresh head/history readbacks; S38 at 476-479 tests coherent persisted winners after paired dispatch. The clean-context gate specifies real write/read/reload evidence, while Polish uses actual key events and named/focus observations and Visual has rendered anchors rather than an unqualified 'looks right'.

Evidence remains scoped: the raw index SHA256 is c5fb62b99ab425667d2346c5475436eaffa42d2f77d389d387edec1f3d3209b8 and all 21 listed artifact hashes match. history-results.json (6af53ad01e0cff5f332417cb8279006fc02c7eed9c457fe99bea91e47c666f84), observations UI.restore_lost_reply_retry, records both committed and retried result at revision 6; S37.restore_retry records revision-4 responses even after revision-5 newer work. runtime-results.json (da795b0a7c722dcd01003b8f7debdb0616fec88f532386d0410ba3a717ab1276), facts S03.completed_stop_preview and S10.js_error_rollback, records before/after displayed input values and restored user-edited-preview-741. These are useful browser-product observations. post-results.json follows an external docker restart, not this exact helper, and does not refute the shared-helper counterexample. The proof-input source hashes match frozen server.js, app.tsx, runtime.ts and runner.html, but Functional prompt/judge hashes changed for the explicit UI-retry addition; the index discloses that sequence. There is no current configured judge execution or measured Oracle/model/portal score, and scripted observations are not presented as that evidence.
counterexample: Broken app that can receive erroneous restart credit: a server keeps current snippets, history and restore-attempt results only in memory and installs a SIGTERM handler that does not exit. It can pass independent-browser reads. On restart_app, the old process continues answering; a replacement fails to bind with EADDRINUSE, but the helper sees the old HTTP responder and returns success. Browser comparisons and a post-'restart' write can all succeed, awarding the four S22 outcomes even though a genuine process restart loses everything. This witness is source-derived and NOT EXERCISED. Conforming alternatives considered independently: an app may preserve a static picture after Stop/error, use an opaque iframe or separate local preview hostname, expose UUID/non-unit revision identities, and serve saved records through rendered HTML. The task-specific wording explicitly accommodates these choices; no additional false failure was established for them.
suggested_fix: Keep this as the deferred shared-harness issue; when the template owner authorizes its repair, make restart success depend on verified old-process exit and a live replacement serving readiness, then run the exact helper against an in-memory SIGTERM-resistant witness and a conforming durable app. Do not patch task-local shared code or weaken the outcomes.
